newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin says saw nothing wrong with Belarus poll.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin says saw nothing wrong with Belarus poll.

text.p: Russia sees nothing unconstitutional about the Belarus referendum which gave majority backing for President Alexander Lukashenko to take sweeping new powers, Interfax news agency quoted a Kremlin spokesman as saying.

"There are no grounds to consider the Belarussian referendum, in the course of which the majority of the population supported the position of President Alexander Lukashenko, as unconstitutional," the spokesman said.

He said Russia assumed that the Belarussian crisis would be defused by political means and added: "Accord and stability of Belarus society will be an important precondition for the further integration of our two countries."

Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin had tried to broker a last-minute agreement between Lukashenko and deputies who said his plans to view the referendum results as binding were unconstitutional. But the deal collapsed after a day.

Lukashenko, who wants to forge a union between the two former Soviet republics, subsequently won a big majority in the poll and he has set up a rival legislature. He has vowed to disband the old parliament.
On Thursday Belarus police barred deputies from entering the main chamber of parliament, allowing them access only to collect their belongings.
